title: Explore the parabola y = a·x² + b·x + c
instructions: Move the sliders to change a, b, c and watch the parabola change. The x-intercepts (where the curve crosses the x-axis) are the ROOTS of the quadratic ax² + bx + c = 0. Try (a, b, c) = (1, −5, 6) for x² − 5x + 6 with roots 2 and 3; (1, −6, 9) for a perfect square with one repeated root; (1, 1, 1) for a parabola that doesn't cross the x-axis (no real roots). Watch how the discriminant b² − 4ac decides the picture.
